headline: High-risk default workspace overlap: Devin can write and exfiltrate while Chatwoot handles customer data, creating leakage, conflict, and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A direct prompt-injection bridge is not documented, but Devin can use MCP, browsers, and shared integrations while Chatwoot exposes APIs and customer-facing content. If Chatwoot outputs are copied into Devin’s workspace or Slack/Linear threads, Devin may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions. The pathway is plausible in default operator workflows, though not proven.
conditions: IF Chatwoot content is pasted or synced into Devin via Slack, Linear, Notion, or MCP
IF Devin is instructed to act on untrusted support transcripts or reports
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of raw support transcripts into Devin
Require a human to strip instructions from Chatwoot outputs before reuse
Use a fixed prompt template that ignores embedded directives
Route Chatwoot exports through a sanitizer step
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, and orders, while Devin has broad network egress, filesystem access, and writes to cloud workspace files. If customer-support artifacts are placed in Devin’s workspace, Devin can transmit them to third-party services or integrations. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default workflows.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is copied into Devin’s workspace or repo clones
IF Devin uses external integrations or browser access on those files
mitigations: Keep customer data out of Devin workspaces
Redact PII before handing artifacts to Devin
Restrict Devin integrations to approved domains only
Review outbound network destinations before each run
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on cloud workspace files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot is a support platform with integrations, and Devin can modify git state, write files, and use shared integrations like GitHub and Slack. If both operate on the same repo, ticket, or workspace, concurrent writes can overwrite each other or create conflicting state. The overlap is broad and dangerous by default when paired in shared operational loops.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository, ticket queue, or Slack thread
IF Chatwoot-triggered tasks cause Devin to edit shared files or git state
mitigations: Assign separate repos or branches per agent
Freeze writes while one agent is active
Use PR-only handoff instead of direct pushes
Limit Devin to read-only access on shared workspaces
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports, and Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on inputs using shell, browser, and write permissions. If Devin treats Chatwoot-derived summaries as authoritative, it may execute incorrect actions or propagate bad facts into commits, tickets, or messages. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF Devin receives Chatwoot summaries, reports, or transcripts as task input
IF no human verification step is inserted before Devin acts
mitigations: Require human review before any Devin action based on Chatwoot output
Use a checklist to verify facts against source systems
Separate summarization from execution roles
Mark Chatwoot outputs as untrusted in task prompts
requires-engineering: add validation gates before write actions

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Devin’s cloud workspace, integrations, and broad egress create a residency and retention mismatch risk if those records are transferred into its environment. The profiles do not show a DPA, residency control, or retention alignment. Because the data class is sensitive and the transfer path is plausible, compliance exposure is high.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is transferred into Devin-managed cloud storage or integrations
IF retention or residency requirements apply to those records
mitigations: Do not move regulated customer records into Devin
Minimize fields before transfer
Confirm residency and retention settings for every integration
Document a DPA and data-flow map before use
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing and retention controls
